title: Postmortem: web blank pages after a font upload
facts: A web deploy uploaded an asset set that was missing two font files; pages that waited on the fonts rendered blank in Safari only.
Lasted 31 minutes, from 19:12 to 19:43 JST; 9 customer reports.
Fixed by re-uploading the complete asset set; the deploy build now fails if the asset manifest lists a file that is not uploaded.
Priya (web engineer) found the missing files by comparing the asset manifest with the bucket listing.

title: Postmortem: SMS sign-in codes delayed in Japan
facts: twilio reported carrier delays for Japanese mobile numbers; sign-in codes arrived 5 to 20 minutes late.
Lasted 1 hour 12 minutes; 1,930 customers signed in with the email fallback during the window.
No change on our side helped; the on-call engineer confirmed the provider incident and wrote it down.
Action item: add a line to the sign-in page telling customers the email option exists (done by Aiko's team).

title: Postmortem: api search index stale for a day
facts: The nightly search index rebuild failed silently; 'find a slot near me' returned results 26 hours old.
Customers saw slots that were already booked; 112 booking attempts failed at the last step with 'slot no longer available'.
Fix: the rebuild job now reports to the job monitor, and an index-freshness panel was added to the api board.
Daniel (api engineer) ran a manual rebuild during working hours; it took 70 minutes.

title: Postmortem: duplicate appointment reminders after a scheduler restart
facts: The notifier scheduler restarted at 02:40 JST during the nightly reminder batch and queued the batch a second time.
8,412 reminders went out twice; 37 customer reports; no reminders were lost.
Fix: every reminder now carries a dedupe key of the form reminder:<booking id>:<date>, and notifier drops a message whose key it has seen in the last 24 hours.
Yuki (notifier engineer) wrote the fix; it shipped on 2024-09-05.

title: Postmortem: bookings an hour off after the US clock change
facts: After the US clock change on 2024-11-03, 1,407 bookings at us-east businesses were shown one hour off in the business dashboard.
Cause: an outdated time zone database in one api image; bookings were stored correctly in UTC, only the display was wrong.
Fixed by updating the time zone data; no booking had to be moved.
Action item: a calendar reminder for the platform team two weeks before every March and November clock change.

title: Postmortem: admin tool session left open on a shared laptop
facts: A support laptop in the office was left signed in to the admin tool overnight; a security review found the open session the next morning.
No accounts were changed or deleted during the open session; the audit log confirmed it.
Admin tool sessions now time out after 2 hours of inactivity instead of 12.
Hana (support lead) changed the support team's shared-laptop rules the same week.

title: Postmortem: partner API certificate expired
facts: The certificate on the partner API name expired at 09:00 JST; partners' systems refused to connect.
Renewal had been failing for a month because the DNS validation record pointed at an old DNS zone; the two-week expiry warnings went to a mailbox nobody read.
Partner API connections failed for 47 minutes; 3 partners were affected.
Ravi renewed the certificate by hand; expiry warnings now go to #platform and page the platform team.

title: Postmortem: CDN purge stuck after the summer campaign release
facts: After a web release for the summer campaign, the cloudflare purge did not complete for 34 minutes; new pages asked for assets the edge did not have and showed broken layouts.
cloudflare later confirmed a delay in their purge pipeline for our region.
The on-call engineer confirmed the purge status in the CDN dashboard and waited; rolling web back would not have helped because the old assets were already purged too.
Action item: the release checklist now waits for the purge to report complete before announcing a campaign.

title: Postmortem: sendgrid daily quota reached during a marketing send
facts: A marketing email was sent through the same sendgrid stream as booking confirmations; the daily quota was reached at 16:40 JST.
Booking confirmations were delayed for about 3 hours until the quota reset; notifier kept them on the queue and sent them all.
Fix: marketing email moved to its own sendgrid stream with its own quota (done on 2025-09-30).
Raising the quota was considered and rejected as a purchasing decision; Tom decided.

title: Postmortem: api audit log writer stopped after a disk filled
facts: The audit writer's local spool disk filled up and the writer stopped; no audit entries were written for 2 hours 5 minutes.
Bookings and accounts kept working the whole time; no customer noticed.
The missing entries were reconstructed from api request logs by Daniel over the next two days; 18,320 entries restored.
Fix: a disk alert for the audit writer and a spool that drops to object storage when the disk passes 70 %.

title: Postmortem: stripe webhooks rejected after the signing secret rotation
facts: Mei rotated the stripe webhook signing secret as planned; the new secret reached the ap-northeast and eu-west nodes but not us-east.
us-east rejected stripe webhooks for 41 minutes; bookings there stayed 'payment pending' longer than usual.
No money moved wrongly: stripe retries webhooks, and every rejected webhook was delivered after the fix.
Fix: the secret is now read from the secrets manager at start-up on every node, with a check that all regions report the same secret version.

title: Postmortem: aws DNS incident in ap-northeast-1
facts: aws reported a DNS resolution incident in ap-northeast-1; api requests from that region failed to resolve internal names for 23 minutes.
us-east and eu-west were unaffected.
Nothing on our side needed to change; the on-call engineer confirmed it on the aws health dashboard and kept the incident thread updated.
Moving traffic out of the region was discussed with the incident commander and decided against because aws reported recovery within 20 minutes.

title: Postmortem: api replica lag double-booked slots in eu-west
facts: Replica lag in eu-west reached 41 seconds during a heavy write burst; slot availability was read from the replica, so 63 slots were booked twice.
Ravi was paged because double bookings needed customer contact, which on-call cannot do.
Fix: availability checks at the final booking step now read from the primary (the feature flag booking_reads_primary, now on everywhere).
Hana's support team contacted all 63 affected customers within a day.

title: Postmortem: notifier queue stalled by a template error
facts: A business name containing an unusual character crashed the confirmation template; each worker crashed on the same message and restarted.
Nothing was delivered for 48 minutes; 2,750 messages were waiting at the peak.
Yuki moved the bad message aside and the queue drained in 15 minutes.
Fix: a message that crashes a worker twice is now moved to a 'parked' queue automatically.

title: web runbook (2024 edition)
facts: This is the 2024 version of the web runbook, before it was merged into the handbook.
web then ran four nodes per region (it is six now).
Board 'Sorrel / web' then had no browser-error panel; front-end errors were read from a separate error tracker.
Rollback for web used the deploy tool's 'Roll back to this' button, about four minutes.

title: notifier runbook (2024 edition)
facts: The 2024 version of the notifier runbook.
notifier then ran two worker nodes per region (it is three now).
The nightly reminder batch for ap-northeast then ran from 01:00 to 03:00 JST (it now runs 02:00 to 04:00).
The duplicate panel did not exist yet; duplicates were found by searching logs.

title: How to rebuild the api search index
facts: Rebuilding the search index is a working-hours job, never a night move for on-call.
A full rebuild takes about 70 minutes; searches keep using the old index until the new one is ready.
Check the index-freshness panel on the api board first; an index under 6 hours old does not need a rebuild.
The rebuild is started from the job console, job 'search-reindex-full', by the api team.

title: How to read the notifier queue panels
facts: Depth alone means nothing; compare 'added per minute' with 'delivered per minute'.
Oldest message age above 30 minutes while delivered per minute is zero means the workers are stuck.
During the nightly reminder batch, depth commonly reaches 1,000 to 1,500 and drains by 06:00 JST.
The parked queue (added 2026-07) is shown on a separate panel; anything there needs Tom's team in working hours.

title: How to purge the CDN by hand
facts: On-call may re-run a purge for web assets from the CDN dashboard; firewall rules are never changed without Aiko.
A normal purge completes within a minute; check its status on the CDN dashboard's purge panel.
Purge by URL prefix, not 'purge everything'; purging everything sends all traffic to the origin at once.
Write the purge id in the incident thread.

title: How to trace one refund through the logs
facts: Search service=payments msg="refund sent" ref=<ref> to see when a refund went to stripe.
A refund has three log lines: requested, sent, settled; settled comes from the stripe webhook and can arrive hours later.
Never search for card numbers; they are never logged.
If one reference shows two 'sent' lines, money may have moved twice: stop and page Mei.

title: How to check replica lag on api
facts: Replica lag is on the 'Database' row of the api board, one line per region.
Normal lag is under 1 second; over 10 seconds for more than a few minutes is worth reading logs about.
Replica lag does not page on its own; it shows up as stale reads.
Promoting a replica is a decision for Ravi, never an on-call move.

title: How to stop a load test that nobody owns
facts: Load test traffic carries the X-Sorrel-Loadtest header and comes from our own address ranges.
Check the game day calendar first; if the test is on it, ask its owner before stopping it.
If nobody owns it, stop it with the load test tool: loadctl stop <test id>, and tell #platform.
In 2026-04 a forgotten soak test ran for 9 hours against api in us-east before anyone noticed.

title: stripe: notes for on-call
facts: stripe retries a webhook it could not deliver for up to 3 days, with growing gaps between attempts.
Disputes arrive as webhooks and are handled by Mei's team in working hours, never by on-call.
Never change anything in the stripe dashboard during an incident; payment settings are Mei's decision.
status.stripe.com is the status page; subscribe the incident thread to it during a payments incident.

title: twilio: Japan carrier notes
facts: Delivery receipts for KDDI numbers in Japan can arrive up to 40 minutes after the SMS was delivered; notifier marks such messages 'pending', not 'failed'.
A pending count rising on the notifier board for KDDI only is usually receipt lag, not failure.
Sender numbers and sending limits are changed by Tom only.
twilio's status page lists Japanese carriers separately; check the carrier line, not only the overall status.

title: sendgrid: quota and streams
facts: The sendgrid daily quota resets at 09:00 JST (00:00 UTC).
Since 2025-09-30 transactional email (confirmations, receipts) and marketing email use separate streams with separate quotas.
Raising the quota is a purchasing decision for Tom, not an on-call action.
When the quota is reached, notifier keeps emails on the queue and sends them after the reset.

title: cloudflare: purge and firewall notes
facts: Purges normally complete within a minute; a purge running for several minutes is a provider-side delay.
The firewall's rate-limit rules for api were raised for the November partner sync season and lowered again on 2025-12-01.
Firewall rules are never changed during an incident without Aiko.
The cloudflare status page lists the Tokyo and Osaka data centres separately.

title: aws: health dashboard and regions
facts: Personal health dashboard notifications for our account are posted automatically in #aws-health.
We run in ap-northeast-1, us-east-1 and eu-west-1; ap-northeast-1 carries the most traffic.
Moving traffic out of a region is decided by the incident commander with the owners of the affected services.
Billing and limit increases go through Ravi.

title: stripe: API version upgrade notes (2026)
facts: payments moved to a newer stripe API version on 2026-07-14 after testing in stripe's test mode for two weeks.
One webhook event type changed its field names; the webhook handler accepts both shapes until 2026-12-31.
Live keys are only in the secrets manager; test keys are in the staging config and never work against live accounts.
Any key seen outside the secrets manager is treated as exposed and goes to Mei.

title: On-call onboarding
facts: New engineers shadow two full shifts before taking a primary shift.
After shadowing, they do a pager drill with Sara: a fake P2 page at an agreed time, acknowledged and handled end to end.
The onboarding checklist has 14 items; the last one is reading the handbook end to end.
Get log search and dashboard access at least a week before the first shadow shift (see 'Access requests for on-call').

title: Alert tuning process
facts: Any alert that should be tuned gets a ticket with the label alert-tuning.
Tickets are reviewed on the first Wednesday of each month in the alert review.
An alert that led only to 'no action' ten times in a month is downgraded to a dashboard or removed.
Alert changes are made by the service owner's team, never during a night shift.

title: Dashboards guide
facts: The board 'Sorrel / Overview' shows one row per service: request rate, error rate, latency.
The board 'Sorrel / On-call' shows pager load: pages per week, pages per night, time to acknowledge.
Every board's time picker defaults to the last hour; widen it before comparing with a deploy.
Do not describe the per-service boards here; they are in the handbook.

title: Access requests for on-call
facts: Log search and dashboard access come with the group oncall-readers.
Request it in #access with a ticket; Kenji approves; it takes one working day.
Paging tool access is set up by the platform team when you join the rotation.
On-call never gets write access to customer data; that is by design.

title: Status page process
facts: Only the incident commander publishes to status.sorrel.app.
On-call drafts the wording in the incident thread using the handbook templates; the commander edits and publishes.
The first public update goes out within 20 minutes of a P1 that customers can see.
Resolved notices stay on the page for 7 days.

title: Game days
facts: Game days are planned exercises; every one is on the game day calendar at least 48 hours ahead.
2025 game days were: 2025-03-12 notifier worker loss, 2025-06-18 api replica failover, 2025-10-15 web node loss.
Alerts during a game day still get acknowledged; the game day owner tells on-call which ones are expected.
Synthetic traffic in a game day carries the X-Sorrel-Loadtest header.

title: Incident commander guide
facts: The incident commander rotation is paged for any P1 still open after 15 minutes.
The commander keeps the timeline, updates the status page, decides who talks to whom, and calls the incident over; the commander does not debug.
Hand the commander role over out loud in the thread: 'Kenji is IC from 03:10'.
After the incident the commander opens the postmortem document and names its author.

title: Postmortem review meeting
facts: The review meets every Thursday at 16:00 JST and is run by the platform team.
Each postmortem gets 30 minutes; the service owner attends.
Action items need an owner and a date before the meeting ends.
Postmortems are blameless: the question is what made the mistake easy and hard to notice.

title: Secrets manager for on-call
facts: Every production credential lives in the secrets manager; on-call can see which secrets exist but not their values.
Never rotate a production credential yourself; rotation is the credential owner's decision.
If a key appears in logs, chat or a ticket: do not copy it anywhere else, link to where it appears, and page the owner of the credential.
Owners: stripe keys Mei; twilio and sendgrid keys Tom; cloudflare Aiko; aws the platform team.
